domain_label: AI-Designed D2C Knitwear — Go-To-Market, Channel Ladder & Demand
purpose: A session-bounded method for the owner of the AI-designed D2C knitwear brand (3-article California line: A1 cotton-blend core, A2 fine-acrylic value front-door, A3 merino/lambswool premium capsule) to design the customer-acquisition and channel system: rank the channel ladder (organic IG/TikTok plus Shopify-owned hub plus email/SMS carry the load, paid social only amplifies proven content, marketplaces secondary and article-specific, never A3 on Amazon), fix the post-de-minimis-repeal bulk-import-then-US-fulfill operating posture as the structurally correct model, set the AOV-and-CAC-headroom test that decides whether an order pays for its own customer, watch the demand signals that govern survival, and pin the [UNKNOWN] Central-Valley-youth hype signal that must be resolved before any name or content calendar ships.
assumptions: no live ad-account or first-party sales dataset exists for this brand; all CAC, conversion, AOV, and return figures are labeled estimates keyed to the brand_market deep-dive and the unit_economics deep-dive, not measured cohort data

the operating model is bulk Importer-of-Record into a California (Turlock) 3PL with domestic last-mile ship; the de-minimis-dependent ship-each-order-direct-from-Ludhiana model is dead and not assumed

the brand seeds in Turlock (~73k value-conscious college town, ~46% Hispanic, CSU Stanislaus) at near-zero CAC and scales to the ship-to-California social shopper where CAC after a volatile-duty landed cost is the single kill-risk
the line is sold premium-led and bundle-driven (AOV target ~$120-150) per the unit_economics verdict; A2 acrylic is a basket-filler and front-door, never a standalone paid-social hero

the price ladder (A2 ~$45-65 / A1 ~$70-95 / A3 ~$120-180) is positioning judgment inherited from the deep-dive, not a margin model; the real contribution floors are owned by the unit_economics layer and re-priced per PO against live duty
the brand has cleared or is clearing an original coined, hype-adjacent, registrable wordmark (classes 25+35); no real athlete/celebrity/event/meme is used as the house brand, a drop, or a SKU
exclusions: the per-article landed-cost stack, the contribution-after-CAC P&L math, and the duty/tariff modeling (owned by the unit_economics KB; consumed here only as the AOV/CAC-headroom precondition)

the final brand name, wordmark, palette, type, and the trademark-clearance gate itself (owned by the naming/identity brand work; this KB only carries the legal-risk guardrail and the hype-signal precondition a name needs)
the AI-design generation pipeline, line plan, size-grading, and tech-pack (owned by the AI-design KB; consumed here only as the organic process-content engine)
yarn, machine, manufacturing, QC, and finishing decisions (owned by the upstream technical specialists)
the make-vs-buy boundary and factory-cost economics (owned by the manufacturing-economics KB)
the final go/no-go viability verdict and the macro decision memo (owned by the decision-brain layer; this KB hands it a hardened channel/GTM read)
source_description: reasoned heuristic-prior estimates for the brand's go-to-market and channel system, grounded in the brand_market sector deep-dive (DEEPDIVE.md sec 1-5): its two-market local-seed-to-social-scale split, its channel ladder (organic plus Shopify hub plus email/SMS carry it, paid amplifies proven content, marketplaces secondary, never A3 on Amazon), its price-ladder positioning judgment, its three story pillars, its naming legal verdict, and its instrument-panel demand signals; reinforced by the unit_economics deep-dive (DEEPDIVE.md sec 4-5,8) for the de-minimis repeal model-flip, the bulk-import-then-US-fulfill posture, the CAC-governs-survival finding, the AOV lever, and the LTV:CAC>3 bar; and the SCOPE_GLOSSARY section 8 D2C vocabulary; no supplied first-party marketing dataset
source_citation: Brand & Market Deep-Dive (FACTORY/sweater_vertical/analysis/brand_market/DEEPDIVE.md sec 1-5 and Open Questions C13); Unit Economics Deep-Dive (FACTORY/sweater_vertical/analysis/unit_economics/DEEPDIVE.md sec 4 de-minimis model-flip, sec 5 contribution-after-CAC P&L and AOV lever, sec 8 go/no-go conditions, sec 9 legal flags); SCOPE_GLOSSARY.md sec 8 (D2C: contribution margin, CAC, AOV, LTV:CAC>3, drop, capsule) and cross-team rule 8; de-minimis repeal EO 14324 effective Aug 29 2025 and MPF $33.58-$651.50 cap [FACT, carried from unit_economics]; US sweater duties cotton 6110.20.20 ~16.5% / wool 6110.11 ~16% / acrylic-MMF 6110.30.30 ~32% [FACT, USITC]; Cal. Civ. Code 3344/3344.1 and Lanham 43(a) right-of-publicity/false-endorsement [FACT]; apparel conversion ~2-3%, blended CAC ~$22 organic-heavy vs ~$75 paid-only, returns ~24-26% online [ESTIMATE, industry-compilation]; heuristic priors where no first-party dataset exists

competency_questions.question: Who is the consumer for this line, and how does the two-market local-seed-to-social-scale split govern every channel choice?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: CONSUMER_TWO_MARKET names the Turlock seed (near-zero-CAC, in-person, ~46% Hispanic, CSU, fixes the size curve) and the ship-to-California social shopper (the scale where CAC is the kill-risk) and states that designing for one market forfeits either cheap trust or all reach

competency_questions.question: What is the ranked channel ladder, and which channels carry the acquisition load versus merely amplify?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: CHANNEL_LADDER ranks organic IG/TikTok plus Shopify-owned hub plus email/SMS as the load-bearing tier, names paid social as amplification-only of proven content, and places marketplaces as secondary/article-specific

competency_questions.question: Why does paid-social-led acquisition at a sub-$90 AOV not survive, and what is the rule that keeps paid in its lane?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: PAID_AMPLIFY_ONLY states that cold paid social at a new-cohort CAC ($45-75 estimate) exceeds the contribution of a sub-$90 single order so paid only amplifies content already proven organically, and ties the rule to the AOV headroom test

competency_questions.question: How does the brand use organic IG/TikTok process content as the earned-reach engine, and what is the brand-ending risk in it?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: ORGANIC_SOCIAL_ENGINE explains the AI-design process content as the TikTok/IG-native earned-media engine and flags that a single public pilling video is brand-ending for the A2 acrylic, so the no-pill promise is a gate not a fake percentage

competency_questions.question: How does the de-minimis repeal force a bulk-import-then-US-fulfill operating posture, and how does that reshape the channel system?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: BULK_IMPORT_FULFILL states that the de-minimis repeal (eff. Aug 29 2025) killed duty-free drop-ship so the brand is a bulk Importer-of-Record into a CA 3PL with domestic ship, reinforced by the MPF cap that punishes per-order import, and that this gates marketplace and channel feasibility

competency_questions.question: What is the price-ladder positioning across the three articles, and which article is the margin engine versus the front door?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: PRICE_LADDER_POSITIONING sets A2 ~$45-65 (acquisition front door), A1 ~$70-95 (margin and LTV engine), A3 ~$120-180 (halo/anchor) as positioning judgment not a model, names A1 the center of gravity, and flags that the front door must not become the whole house

competency_questions.question: How is AOV pushed above ~$90 to create CAC headroom, and what is the formula that tests whether an order pays for its own customer?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: AOV_CAC_HEADROOM recomputes per-order contribution from AOV minus all variable costs minus blended CAC, derives the max-CAC ceiling and the bundle uplift that lifts AOV to ~$120-150, and the formula recomputes from its labeled inputs

competency_questions.question: How is the marketplace question decided per article, and why is A3 never put on Amazon?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: MARKETPLACE_SECONDARY routes Etsy/TikTok-Shop to the youth A2 capsule and Amazon only to a basic A1/A2 cash line, blocks A3 from Amazon because it commoditizes the premium/AI story, and gates wholesale on a confirmed margin floor

competency_questions.question: What demand signals must the owner watch every cycle, and which one is owned by no upstream file?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: DEMAND_SIGNALS enumerates conversion, return rate by article and size, A2 pilling sentiment, sell-through by hero colour, waitlist depth, and the live duty/de-minimis state, and HYPE_SIGNAL_PIN flags the Central-Valley-youth hype signal as the [UNKNOWN] owned by no file

competency_questions.question: How is the naming legal risk kept off the channel and content plan without owning the naming decision itself?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: NAMING_LEGAL_GUARDRAIL states the hard no on a real athlete/celebrity/event/meme as the house brand, drop, or SKU (3344/3344.1 plus Lanham 43(a) plus class-25 marks stack, NIL closes the local-kid loophole), and requires an original coined hype-adjacent registrable name before any content or paid spend references it

competency_questions.question: How is blended CAC held under the survival threshold, and what acquisition mix does that force?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: CAC_DISCIPLINE holds blended CAC under ~$35 (organic-heavy), forces acquisition to lean organic/community/affiliate/owner-audience over cold paid social, and ties the threshold to the LTV:CAC>3 bar and the AOV headroom test

competency_questions.question: How is the whole GTM system assembled into one launch plan and kept alive against trend, duty, and CAC drift?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: GTM_PLAN integrates the channel ladder, operating posture, price ladder, AOV/CAC test, and signals into one launch artifact, and GTM_REVIEW_LOOP sets the cadence and the triggers (trend shift, duty change, CAC drift, pilling event) that re-run the plan

glossary.definition: The ranked acquisition stack for this brand: organic IG/TikTok content plus the Shopify-owned hub plus the email/SMS list carry the load; paid social only amplifies content already proven to perform organically; marketplaces are secondary and article-specific; wholesale is a later pilot gated on a confirmed margin floor.

The two-market posture: Turlock (~73k value-conscious college town, ~46% Hispanic, CSU Stanislaus) cheaply seeds the first 200-500 customers in person and fixes the size curve, but the business only reaches meaningful scale through the ship-to-California social shopper, where contribution margin after CAC is the single kill-risk.

The rule that paid social is used solely to scale a piece of content that has already proven organic performance, never to buy cold customers; cold paid-social acquisition at a new-cohort CAC ($45-75 estimate) does not survive a sub-$90 single-order AOV on the contribution math.

The structurally forced operating model after the de-minimis ($800) repeal (eff. Aug 29 2025): the brand is a bulk Importer of Record paying duty once on a bulk entry into a California (Turlock) 3PL, then ships domestic last-mile; the MPF $33.58-$651.50 cap rewards the single bulk entry and punishes per-order import, killing the duty-free drop-ship model.

The amount of contribution an order yields before customer-acquisition cost is subtracted; pushing AOV above ~$90 (toward a ~$120-150 bundle or premium target) is the lever that creates room for a realistic CAC to be paid and still leave per-order profit.

Total acquisition spend divided by new customers across all channels; for this brand the survival threshold is under ~$35, achievable only organic-heavy (~$22 estimate) because a cold-paid-only mix runs ~$75 (estimate) and exceeds the line's contribution on a sub-$90 order.

Architecture rule: the A1 cotton core is the margin-and-LTV engine (longest sell-window, best repeat, low-duty), sitting behind the A2 fine-acrylic value front door that drives youth reach and UGC; if the transient front door visually or verbally becomes the house brand, both margin and brand longevity erode.

The consumer claim that the garment will not pill, made by promising the contractual ICI pilling-box gate (>=3-4 post-wash) and never a fabricated percentage; a single public pilling video on TikTok is brand-ending for the A2 acrylic, so the claim must be defensible by the QC gate, not by marketing-speak.

An original, coined, arbitrary-or-suggestive wordmark that captures California/youth/sport-adjacent energy and current-hype tempo without referencing any real person, team, league, event, or meme; it is registrable and ownable, the opposite of a borrowed identity that can be yanked or sued.

What is actually trending for Central Valley youth in 2026 and where exactly they get their news; a genuine [UNKNOWN] owned by no upstream file, yet the required live input to both a hype-adjacent name and trend-native content, which must be pinned before any name or content calendar ships.

A CAC, conversion, AOV, or return figure built as an industry-compilation benchmark times this brand's configuration, explicitly tagged estimate with method, basis, and confidence, and never asserted as a measured first-party cohort number; the single hardening move is a live $1-2k ad test.

nodes.definition: Pin down the consumer and the two-market posture that governs the whole GTM plan: Market 1 is Turlock, a ~73k value-conscious college town (~46% Hispanic, ~41% White, CSU Stanislaus ~10.5k students) that is the cheapest place on earth to acquire the first 200-500 customers at near-zero CAC through pop-ups, weekend markets, CSU channels, and the community graph, and to fix the size curve in person (every offline fitting buys down the online return rate). Market 2 is the ship-to-California social shopper, the young value-quality knit buyer who discovers product on TikTok FYP / IG Reels / Pinterest, where the business only reaches meaningful scale and where contribution margin after CAC is the single kill-risk. The posture local-seed-to-social-scale falls out: designing for only one market forfeits either cheap trust or all reach.

included: the Turlock seed and the ship-to-CA scale consumer
the size-curve-fix and near-zero-CAC seed mechanism
the local-seed-to-social-scale posture
excluded: the channel ladder ranking itself
the national TAM/SAM number (refused, [UNKNOWN])

pros.claim: Naming the two markets distinctly prevents spending scale-channel money to reach the seed and seed-channel effort to reach the scale market
pros.example: running CSU pop-ups for the first 300 customers and a size-curve read instead of buying cold TikTok ads before a single fit is calibrated

cons.claim: Over-investing in the cheap Turlock seed can mistake an order-of-magnitude-small local market (~$50-110k/yr) for the business
cons.example: scaling local pop-up cadence as if it were the growth engine when the business only exists at social scale

failure_modes: treating the local seed's near-zero CAC as the scale-market CAC and under-budgeting acquisition
skipping the in-person size-curve fix so the online return rate runs uncalibrated from day one
acceptance_tests: the split names the Turlock seed (near-zero CAC, size-curve fix, ~46% Hispanic, CSU) and the ship-to-CA social shopper (scale, CAC kill-risk) and states that single-market design forfeits trust or reach
revisit_triggers: the seed customer count or the size-curve read materially shifts
the scale-market discovery surface (TikTok/IG/Pinterest) changes

base.update_signal: the seed/scale split or the discovery surface changes

nodes.definition: Establish the operating posture the de-minimis repeal forces before any channel is chosen: the duty-free <$800 de-minimis exemption was suspended for all countries effective Aug 29 2025 (EO 14324), so the ship-each-order-direct-from-Ludhiana duty-free model is dead. The brand must be a bulk Importer of Record paying full MFN duty plus the India surcharge once on a bulk entry into a California (Turlock) 3PL, then ship domestic last-mile. The MPF cap ($33.58 floor to $651.50 ceiling per formal entry) independently rewards the single bulk entry and punishes per-order import, so the fee structure alone reinforces bulk before a cent of duty. This posture is the structural precondition that gates marketplace feasibility, working-capital profile, and where the brand carries inventory risk.

included: the de-minimis-repeal model-flip to bulk IOR into a CA 3PL
the MPF-cap reinforcement of bulk over per-order
the posture as a precondition gating channels
excluded: the per-article landed-cost stack and contribution math (unit_economics owns)
the working-capital cash-cycle modeling (unit_economics owns)

pros.claim: Fixing the bulk-import posture up front stops the channel plan from assuming a zero-inventory drop-ship model that no longer legally or economically exists
pros.example: planning a CA 3PL bulk receipt and domestic ship instead of a TikTok-Shop integration that drop-ships parcels from Ludhiana

cons.claim: Bulk import pre-commits cash to inventory and a 3PL minimum, raising the launch capital and the markdown risk versus the dead drop-ship fantasy
cons.example: a dye-lot MOQ forcing hundreds of units of cash out per colour before the first order ships

failure_modes: designing a channel or marketplace flow that assumes duty-free per-order import
paying the MPF floor on many tiny entries by shipping direct instead of one bulk entry
acceptance_tests: the posture states de-minimis is repealed (eff. Aug 29 2025), that the model is bulk IOR into a CA 3PL with domestic ship, and that the MPF cap rewards bulk and punishes per-order import
revisit_triggers: a change in de-minimis enforcement or the MPF cap
the India duty surcharge level shifts at a PO cycle

base.update_signal: a de-minimis, MPF, or duty rule that reshapes the fulfillment model changes

nodes.definition: Rank the acquisition channels into the ladder the deep-dive prescribes rather than defaulting to paid ads: the load-bearing tier is organic IG/TikTok content plus the Shopify-owned hub plus the email/SMS list; paid social sits one rung down as amplification-only of content already proven organically; marketplaces are secondary and article-specific; wholesale is a later pilot gated on a confirmed margin floor. The ladder is ordered by contribution survivability, not by reach: organic carries the load because it is the only acquisition cheap enough to clear the sub-$90-AOV contribution math, and every paid or marketplace rung is conditioned on the organic engine working first. This ranking is the spine every downstream channel node builds from.

included: the ordered ladder organic+hub+email/SMS > paid-amplify > marketplace > wholesale
the ordering-by-contribution-survivability rationale
the conditioning of each paid rung on the organic engine
excluded: the internal mechanics of each individual channel
the AOV/CAC arithmetic itself

pros.claim: An explicit contribution-ordered ladder stops the default mistake of leading with paid ads that the sub-$90 order cannot pay for
pros.example: the owner building an organic process-content cadence and an email list before turning on a single dollar of paid amplification

cons.claim: An organic-first ladder is slower to scale and depends on content hitting, which is not guaranteed for a no-name brand
cons.example: a launch quarter where no piece of content breaks out and there is no paid lever proven enough to amplify

failure_modes: inverting the ladder and leading with cold paid social at a sub-$90 AOV
treating marketplaces as a primary channel instead of an article-specific secondary
acceptance_tests: the ladder ranks organic+hub+email/SMS as load-bearing, paid social as amplify-only, and marketplaces as secondary/article-specific, ordered by contribution survivability
revisit_triggers: a channel's CAC or contribution economics shift the optimal order
the organic engine proves it can or cannot carry the load

base.update_signal: a channel's economics reorders the ladder

nodes.definition: Set up organic IG/TikTok as the earned-reach engine that carries acquisition: the AI-design pipeline is genuinely novel and is TikTok/IG-native process content (AI-designed, made by hands, built to last), the story engine that translates runway/trend into platform-native process video. This is the only acquisition channel cheap enough to keep blended CAC under ~$35, so it is load-bearing, not supplemental. It runs on the brand's three story pillars and feeds the owned hub and list. The binding risk lives here: a single public pilling video on TikTok is brand-ending for the A2 acrylic, so the no-pill claim must be promised as the contractual ICI pilling gate (>=3-4 post-wash), never a fabricated percentage, and the content must not over-promise what the QC gate cannot defend.

included: AI-design process content as the earned-media engine
the pilling-video brand-ending risk and the gate-not-percentage promise
feeding the owned hub and list
excluded: the AI-design generation pipeline itself (AI-design KB owns)

pros.claim: Organic process content is genuinely novel earned media that acquires customers at a CAC paid social cannot match, and is the only channel that keeps the contribution math alive
pros.example: a process reel of the AI-design-to-hand-knit pipeline breaking out and driving owned-hub traffic at near-zero marginal cost

cons.claim: Earned reach is unreliable and slow, and a single quality misstep on camera can do outsized damage
cons.example: a customer-posted pilling video on the acrylic A2 undoing months of organic brand-building overnight

failure_modes: promising a fabricated anti-pill percentage the QC gate cannot defend and triggering returns and a pilling-video event
treating organic as a nice-to-have rather than the load-bearing acquisition channel
acceptance_tests: organic process content is set up as the load-bearing earned-media engine with the no-pill claim promised as the QC gate and the pilling-video risk explicitly managed
revisit_triggers: a pilling-sentiment or quality event surfaces on social

base.update_signal: organic performance or a pilling-sentiment event changes

nodes.definition: Set up the owned channels that convert earned reach into repeat revenue and protect the brand from platform risk: the Shopify-owned hub as the transaction and brand home, and the email/SMS list as the owned repeat-purchase channel the brand controls outright. Organic social discovers; the owned hub and list retain. Because CAC is paid once per customer and the LTV:CAC>3 bar depends on repeat, the list is where lifetime value is actually built and where the A1 cotton core's repeat economics are realized. The owned channel also insulates the brand from an algorithm change that could zero out organic reach overnight, making it the durable asset behind the volatile social front.

included: the Shopify hub as transaction/brand home
the email/SMS list as the owned repeat channel
the insulation from platform/algorithm risk
excluded: the discovery content that feeds it (organic node owns)
the contribution math the repeat feeds into

pros.claim: An owned hub and list turn one-time discovered buyers into repeat customers the brand reaches at near-zero marginal CAC, the only way LTV:CAC>3 is reached
pros.example: an email/SMS flow driving a second A1 cotton purchase from a customer first acquired by an organic reel, amortizing the original CAC

cons.claim: List-building is slow and a small early list yields little repeat, so it cannot carry the launch alone
cons.example: a launch quarter where the list is too thin to generate meaningful repeat revenue yet

failure_modes: renting the audience on a marketplace or platform instead of owning the hub and list
neglecting the list so no repeat-purchase channel exists to clear the LTV:CAC bar
acceptance_tests: the Shopify hub and the email/SMS list are set up as the owned repeat-and-retention layer that realizes the A1 repeat economics and insulates against platform risk
revisit_triggers: list growth or repeat-purchase rate materially changes
a platform/algorithm change threatens organic reach

base.update_signal: list growth, repeat rate, or platform reach changes

nodes.definition: Constrain paid social to amplification of proven content only, never cold acquisition. The contribution math is the reason: a new-cohort 2025-26 apparel CAC of ~$45-75 (estimate, industry-compilation, MED confidence) is the same order of magnitude as the entire gross margin, so cold paid social at a sub-$90 single-order AOV loses money on the first order and does not survive. Paid is therefore used only to scale a piece of content that has already proven organic performance and a configuration (premium or bundle) that clears the AOV/CAC-headroom test. The rule keeps paid in its lane: it multiplies a working signal, it does not manufacture demand at a CAC the order cannot pay.

included: the amplify-only constraint on paid social
the sub-$90-AOV cold-paid-does-not-survive finding
conditioning paid on proven content and a headroom-clearing config
excluded: the AOV/CAC formula itself (headroom node owns)
the organic content production

pros.claim: Restricting paid to amplification prevents the single most expensive GTM mistake: buying cold customers at a CAC the order cannot recover
pros.example: putting paid spend only behind a reel already converting organically on a $130 bundle rather than on a cold $55 A2 single

cons.claim: An amplify-only rule caps paid-driven growth speed and leaves the brand dependent on organic content actually breaking out first
cons.example: no content proven enough to amplify in a quarter, so paid stays dark and growth stalls

failure_modes: turning on cold paid social at a sub-$90 AOV and losing money per first order
amplifying a converting reel that points at a money-losing single-unit config instead of a bundle
acceptance_tests: paid social is constrained to amplifying proven content on a headroom-clearing config, with the sub-$90-AOV cold-paid-does-not-survive reason stated
revisit_triggers: a live ad test hardens or collapses the CAC band
a content piece proves organic performance worth amplifying

base.update_signal: the realized CAC band or proven-content availability changes

nodes.definition: Decide marketplaces as a secondary, article-specific channel, never the primary acquisition path and never a home for the premium story. Etsy and TikTok-Shop fit the youth A2 capsule for reach and UGC; Amazon is allowed only for a basic A1/A2 cash line; A3 merino is never put on Amazon because the marketplace commoditizes the premium and AI-design story that is the brand's whole defensible position. Each marketplace must also clear the bulk-import operating posture (no duty-free drop-ship) and its own fee/return economics. The node routes each article to the marketplaces that fit it and blocks the ones that would erode it.

acceptance_tests: each article is routed to or blocked from each marketplace per the rules (A2 to Etsy/TikTok-Shop, basic A1/A2 to Amazon, A3 never on Amazon), each gated on the bulk-import posture

nodes.definition: Treat wholesale (Faire / boutique) as a deferred pilot, not a launch channel, gated on a confirmed unit-margin floor from the unit_economics layer. Wholesale halves the realized price (a boutique buys at roughly keystone), so it only clears if landed cost plus the wholesale discount still leaves contribution, which is [UNKNOWN] until the landed cost is fixed against live duty. The pilot is piloted only after the contribution floor is confirmed, and is best suited to the A1 core and A3 halo where the per-unit margin can absorb the wholesale haircut, not the thin A2. It is the lowest rung of the ladder because it forfeits the owned-customer relationship and the D2C margin the whole plan is built on.

excluded: the landed-cost computation (unit_economics owns)

pros.claim: Gating wholesale on a confirmed margin floor prevents launching a channel that loses money once the keystone discount hits the landed cost
pros.example: deferring a Faire listing until the unit_economics landed cost confirms an A1 unit survives the wholesale haircut

cons.claim: Deferring wholesale forgoes an early reach and cash-flow channel that boutiques could have provided
cons.example: a boutique buyer interested at launch turned away because the margin floor is not yet confirmed

failure_modes: piloting wholesale before the margin floor is confirmed and selling below contribution
wholesaling the thin A2 whose margin cannot absorb the keystone haircut
acceptance_tests: wholesale is held as a deferred pilot gated on a confirmed unit-margin floor, scoped to A1/A3, with the keystone-haircut feasibility stated
revisit_triggers: the unit_economics layer confirms or denies a wholesale margin floor

base.update_signal: the wholesale margin floor is confirmed or a boutique opportunity arises

nodes.definition: Set the three-article price ladder as positioning judgment (not a margin model; the contribution floors are owned by unit_economics and re-priced per PO against live duty): A2 fine-acrylic ~$45-65 as the acquisition / youth front door, A1 cotton core ~$70-95 as the margin-and-LTV engine, A3 merino/lambswool ~$120-180 as the halo / press / price-anchor. The A1 cotton core is the center of gravity: comparable base duty to wool (cotton 6110.20.20 ~16.5% vs wool 6110.11 ~16%; acrylic/MMF 6110.30.30 ~32% is the outlier the border penalizes), the longest sell-window (~Sept-April), and the best repeat-purchase LTV. The architecture rule binds the ladder: transient youth energy goes at the front as acquisition, the durable margin-bearing A1 sits behind and must be protected, and the A2 front door must not become the whole house.

included: the A2/A1/A3 price-positioning ladder
A1 as margin engine vs A2 as front door
the duty context (cotton ~16.5% ~ wool ~16%, acrylic ~32% outlier)
excluded: the contribution-margin floors and the duty model (unit_economics owns)
the AOV/CAC arithmetic

pros.claim: A clear price ladder with A1 as the protected center of gravity keeps the margin engine from being cannibalized by the cheap front door
pros.example: pricing A1 at ~$80 as the repeat-LTV core while A2 at ~$55 drives youth reach but is never positioned as the house brand

cons.claim: These are positioning bands not contribution floors, so reading them as a margin model overstates what the price alone proves
cons.example: treating the A2 ~$55 band as profitable when, post-duty and CAC, it loses money as a standalone unit

failure_modes: letting the A2 youth front door visually or verbally become the house brand and eroding margin and longevity
treating the price bands as a margin model rather than positioning judgment
acceptance_tests: the ladder sets A2 ~$45-65 (front door), A1 ~$70-95 (margin engine, center of gravity), A3 ~$120-180 (halo), tagged positioning-not-a-model, with A1's duty/sell-window/LTV basis

nodes.definition: Set the positioning that splits the competitive field and the three story pillars that carry organic content: never fight on the axis you lose. Against fast-fashion (Shein/H&M-tier) win on durability, fit, no-pill, story, and local trust, never on price; against premium (Everlane/Quince/J.Crew-tier) win on price-for-quality plus AI-design novelty plus local authenticity plus limited drops, never try to out-luxury. The three pillars are: (1) AI-designed, made by hands, built to last (the novel, TikTok/IG-native process-content engine, novelty in-house not in a borrowed face); (2) no-prickle, no-pill, holds its shape (the QC pilling gate turned into a promise, never a fake percentage); (3) from Turlock, for the way California actually dresses (the warm-climate constraint turned into a clean/light/Californian asset, never alpine heritage-wool). The identity must not hard-code a fibre or a season.

included: the split-the-field positioning vs fast-fashion and premium
the three story pillars
the no-fibre/no-season identity rule
excluded: the final identity system (palette/type/photography; naming KB owns)
the legal naming guardrail (its own node)

pros.claim: Splitting the field keeps the brand from competing on the axis it loses and gives organic content a defensible, true story
pros.example: marketing A1 on durability/fit/no-pill against Shein rather than trying to match Shein on price

cons.claim: A story leaning on no-pill and AI-design over-promises if the QC gate or the pipeline cannot back the claim on camera
cons.example: a built-to-last claim contradicted by a customer pilling video, converting the story into a liability

failure_modes: fighting fast-fashion on price or premium on luxury, the two losing axes
hard-coding a fibre or season into the identity so the warm-climate line is boxed in
acceptance_tests: positioning splits fast-fashion (win on durability/fit/no-pill/story/local, never price) from premium (win on price-for-quality/AI/local/drops, never out-luxury) and the three pillars are stated with the no-fibre/no-season rule
revisit_triggers: a competitor or category shift changes the winning axis
a quality or pipeline event undercuts a pillar

base.update_signal: the competitive axis or a story-pillar's defensibility changes

nodes.definition: The formula node that recomputes per-order contribution and the CAC ceiling from an order's AOV, so the GTM plan can test whether an order pays for its own customer, with every input a labeled estimate (never a measured figure). Compute: variable-cost subtotal per order = landed COGS (from unit_economics, ~$11 A1/A2, ~$20 A3) + payment processing (2.9% of AOV + $0.30) + outbound ship-to-customer (~$7-8/order) + returns reserve (~22-26% of orders carried as a per-order load) ; then pre-CAC contribution = AOV - variable-cost subtotal ; then post-CAC contribution = pre-CAC contribution - blended CAC ; then the max-CAC ceiling = pre-CAC contribution (the CAC at which the first order breaks even), and the LTV:CAC>3 allowable CAC = (pre-CAC contribution x repeat orders) / 3. Because landed COGS, returns, and CAC all enter as bands, the output is a BAND, not a single number; it tightens once a live $1-2k ad test hardens the CAC. The shared assumptions (Shopify 2.9%+$0.30, returns ~22-26%, ship ~$7-8, CAC ~$22 organic-heavy to ~$75 paid-only) make the band reproducible, not authoritative; cold paid at a sub-$90 AOV yields a negative post-CAC contribution, which is exactly why paid is amplify-only and AOV must be pushed past ~$90.

included: the per-order contribution and CAC-ceiling recomputation from AOV
the LTV:CAC>3 allowable-CAC derivation
the band-output-tightens-with-an-ad-test discipline
excluded: the full landed-cost stack and P&L (unit_economics owns; consumed as an input band)
the bundle construction itself (bundle node owns)

pros.claim: A recomputable headroom formula converts the abstract CAC-governs-survival rule into a per-config go/no-go an owner can apply to any AOV
pros.example: showing a $55 A2 single yields negative post-CAC contribution at $45 CAC while a $130 bundle survives to ~$69 CAC

cons.claim: The formula is only as good as its band inputs, and landed COGS plus CAC are both soft estimates until a live test lands
cons.example: a CAC band off by 50% flips an article from marginal to losing, so the output reads more precise than the evidence supports

failure_modes: treating the band output as a measured forecast instead of a labeled estimate that needs an ad test
omitting returns or ship from the variable stack and overstating contribution
acceptance_tests: the formula subtracts landed COGS, payment, ship, and returns from AOV for pre-CAC contribution, subtracts blended CAC for post-CAC, derives the max-CAC ceiling and the LTV:CAC>3 allowable CAC, and outputs a band that tightens when CAC is tested
revisit_triggers: a live ad test hardens the CAC band
the landed COGS, returns, or ship input bands shift

base.update_signal: an ad test or an input band changes the contribution/ceiling output

nodes.definition: Set the bundling lever that lifts AOV above ~$90 toward the ~$120-150 target, the single move that makes the line close. CAC and outbound shipping are charged per order, not per unit, so a two-unit bundle (e.g. 2 x ~$65 avg) or a one-premium-unit order amortizes one CAC and one ship over a bigger basket: a ~$130 AOV survives a CAC up to ~$69 and clears LTV:CAC>3 at ~$57 with modest repeat, versus a single $55 A2 that dies at ~$23. The central pricing instruction is therefore to sell the line in baskets >= ~$120 (two units or one premium unit), never as single $55 sweaters. A2 acrylic is used deliberately as a low-margin basket-filler inside bundles, never a standalone hero, and A3 premium or a deliberate two-piece bundle is the AOV target that creates CAC headroom.

included: the bundle/premium AOV uplift to ~$120-150
the per-order amortization of one CAC and one ship
A2-as-basket-filler not standalone hero
excluded: the headroom formula itself (its own node)
the contribution P&L (unit_economics owns)

pros.claim: Bundling amortizes one CAC and one ship over a larger basket, lifting the survivable CAC from ~$23 on a single to ~$69 on a $130 bundle
pros.example: a two-piece A1+A2 bundle at ~$130 AOV that survives a realistic $45-70 CAC where the A2 single never could

cons.claim: Bundling can depress conversion or invite higher returns if the second unit is a poor fit, and discounting the bundle erodes the contribution it was meant to protect
cons.example: a deep bundle discount that lifts AOV but cuts per-unit contribution below the single-unit margin

failure_modes: selling single $55 A2 units at a sub-$90 AOV that cannot pay a realistic CAC
discounting a bundle so hard it erases the AOV-headroom benefit
acceptance_tests: the lever sets an AOV target of ~$120-150 via two-unit or one-premium baskets, shows the per-order CAC/ship amortization, and casts A2 as a bundle-filler not a standalone hero
revisit_triggers: bundle conversion or attach rate is measured
a CAC or contribution shift changes the required AOV target

base.update_signal: bundle conversion/attach or the required AOV target changes

nodes.definition: Hold blended CAC under the survival threshold and force the acquisition mix that achieves it. The unit_economics verdict is that the brand only closes if blended CAC stays under ~$35, which for a no-name brand means acquisition cannot come mostly from cold paid social (new 2025-26 cohorts pay ~$45-75 estimate); it must lean organic / community / affiliate / owner-audience, holding paid to <=~35-40% of the mix. This is a go-to-market precondition, not a nicety, and the single most consequential lever in the whole stack: it ties directly to the LTV:CAC>3 bar (allowable CAC depends on pre-CAC contribution and repeat) and to the AOV-headroom test. The whole verdict rests on a single un-cross-examined CAC benchmark, so one live $1-2k ad test is the highest-leverage data the owner can buy.

included: the <~$35 blended-CAC threshold and the organic-heavy mix it forces
the paid <=35-40% mix cap
the live-ad-test as the single hardening move
excluded: the contribution P&L (unit_economics owns)
the organic content production (organic node owns)

pros.claim: A hard blended-CAC threshold and an organic-heavy mix is the one lever that flips the line from money-losing to viable
pros.example: holding paid to ~35% and leaning organic/community to keep blended CAC near $25 so A1 and bundles clear LTV:CAC>3

cons.claim: An organic-heavy mix caps growth speed and the CAC threshold itself rests on a single un-tested benchmark that could be wrong in either direction
cons.example: a real CAC above $35 even with an organic-heavy mix, which only a live ad test would reveal

failure_modes: letting cold paid social dominate the mix and pushing blended CAC over ~$35
treating the CAC threshold as proven rather than a single-benchmark estimate needing an ad test
acceptance_tests: blended CAC is held under ~$35 with paid <=~35-40% of the mix, tied to the LTV:CAC>3 bar, and the live $1-2k ad test is named as the single hardening move
revisit_triggers: a live ad test returns a real blended CAC
the acquisition mix or repeat rate shifts the allowable CAC

base.update_signal: a live ad test or a mix change moves the blended CAC

nodes.definition: Manage the return rate that quietly erases a thin contribution, splitting it by article and by size. Online apparel returns run far higher than in-store (carry ~24-26% online vs ~6% in-store; hold the gap, online >> offline is robust, the decimal is soft), and a fine-gauge fit-sensitive sweater is high-return by category. The two levers are: (1) the Turlock in-person seed that fixes the size curve before scale, because every garment fitted offline buys down the online return rate; (2) splitting the return signal by article and by size, since the size curve is [UNKNOWN] until pop-ups run. Returns enter the AOV/CAC formula as a per-order variable cost, so an uncontrolled return rate directly raises the CAC ceiling the order must clear.

included: the ~24-26% online return rate (gap robust, decimal soft)
the size-curve fix via the Turlock seed
splitting returns by article and size
excluded: the returns-reserve dollar modeling (unit_economics owns)
the contribution P&L

pros.claim: Fixing the size curve in person and splitting returns by article and size cuts the single most under-watched contribution drain
pros.example: calibrating the size grade at CSU pop-ups so the online A1 return rate runs below the fine-gauge category default

cons.claim: The exact return rate is unknown for this fit/fabric until first-cohort data, so the per-order returns load is a soft estimate
cons.example: a fine-gauge fit running returns above the 24-26% carried band, compressing contribution more than modeled

failure_modes: carrying a single blended return rate instead of splitting by article and size
scaling online before the in-person size curve is calibrated and eating a high uncalibrated return rate
acceptance_tests: returns are carried at ~24-26% online (gap robust, decimal soft), split by article and size, with the Turlock size-curve fix named as the buy-down lever
revisit_triggers: first-cohort return data by article and size arrives
the pop-up size-curve calibration completes

base.update_signal: first-cohort return data or the size-curve calibration changes

nodes.definition: Enumerate the demand signals that decide survival and must be watched every cycle; direction is solid, magnitude is soft (niche-blended industry compilations, not this brand's numbers). The panel: blended CAC (organic-heavy ~$22 vs paid-only ~$75 estimate); contribution after CAC, not gross margin, as the viability test (LTV:CAC>3); conversion ~2-3% apparel with cart-abandon ~70%; return rate ~24-26% online vs ~6% in-store split by article and size; A2 pilling sentiment on social; sell-through by hero colour (the line is colour-starved, ~2-4 launch colours, so the hero-colour signal is load-bearing); pre-order/waitlist depth; and the live duty plus de-minimis state every order cycle. The panel is the input that triggers the review loop and feeds every channel and pricing decision; it explicitly excludes the one signal no upstream file owns (the hype signal, its own node).

included: the instrument-panel signals (CAC, conversion, returns, pilling sentiment, hero-colour sell-through, waitlist, live duty)
the direction-solid-magnitude-soft caveat
feeding the review loop
excluded: the Central-Valley-youth hype signal (its own pin node)
the contribution P&L math

pros.claim: A defined instrument panel catches a survival signal drifting before it compresses contribution for a whole season
pros.example: watching hero-colour sell-through on a colour-starved line and re-weighting the next drop's 2-4 colours toward the winner

cons.claim: The benchmark magnitudes are industry compilations not this brand's numbers, so a panel read can mislead if treated as measured
cons.example: anchoring on a 2-3% conversion benchmark when the no-name brand's real conversion is materially lower at launch

failure_modes: watching gross margin instead of contribution-after-CAC as the viability test
ignoring the live duty/de-minimis state in the panel and being surprised by a landed-cost swing
acceptance_tests: the panel lists CAC, contribution-after-CAC, conversion, returns by article/size, pilling sentiment, hero-colour sell-through, waitlist depth, and live duty state, tagged direction-solid-magnitude-soft
revisit_triggers: a panel signal crosses a threshold
a new first-party data source replaces an industry benchmark

base.update_signal: a panel signal crosses a threshold or a benchmark is replaced by first-party data

nodes.definition: Pin the one demand input owned by no upstream file: what is actually trending for Central Valley youth in 2026 and where exactly they get their news. The demand side treats it as a translation problem and the naming side hands it back, so no file pins it, yet it is the required live input to both a hype-adjacent name and trend-native content. It is a genuine [UNKNOWN] and a first-class open question, not a refusal to research; it must be resolved (via the trend-ingestion pass / AI-design layer) before any brand name or content calendar ships. The binding instruction is a gate: do not let a name or a content calendar ship before this signal is pinned, because both the hype-adjacent wordmark and the organic content cadence depend on it.

included: the [UNKNOWN] Central-Valley-youth hype-and-news signal
the gate blocking a name or content calendar until it is pinned
the hand-off to the trend-ingestion / AI-design layer
excluded: the final name itself (naming KB owns)
the broader demand panel (its own node)

pros.claim: Naming the hype signal as a first-class [UNKNOWN] gate prevents shipping a name or content calendar on a guessed trend that no file actually owns
pros.example: holding the wordmark filing and the content calendar until a trend-ingestion pass pins what Turlock youth are actually watching

cons.claim: Treating it as a hard gate can stall launch if the signal is slow to pin, and the signal is fast-moving once captured
cons.example: a launch delayed waiting on a hype read that shifts again before the content ships

failure_modes: shipping a hype-adjacent name or a trend-native content calendar before the signal is pinned
assuming an upstream file owns the signal when none does
acceptance_tests: the hype signal is flagged as the [UNKNOWN] owned by no file, gating any name or content calendar until pinned, with the hand-off to the trend-ingestion / AI-design layer named

nodes.definition: Carry the binding legal guardrail that keeps the channel and content plan off a name that can be sued or yanked, without owning the naming decision itself. The hard no: do NOT name the brand, a drop, or a SKU after a real athlete, celebrity, nickname, team, league, or event. Four bodies of law stack and any one is enough to lose: California Civil Code 3344 right of publicity (the greater of $750 or actual damages, plus the infringer's profits, plus punitives, plus, decisively, the prevailing party's attorneys' fees, which can exceed the line's whole margin); 3344.1 post-mortem right (descendible 70 years); Lanham Act 43(a) false endorsement (actionable with no registration required to sue); and Class-25 apparel trademark (athletes register and enforce their names; the Giannis Greek Freak matter reportedly settled ~$2M). NIL closes the just-a-local-kid loophole; the dead are not a safe harbor. The safe path is an original coined, hype-ADJACENT, registrable wordmark; a cleared non-identity meme can be a drop name at most. No content or paid spend may reference a name before it clears.

included: the hard no on real athlete/celebrity/event/meme as house brand, drop, or SKU
the 3344/3344.1/Lanham 43(a)/Class-25 stack and NIL/post-mortem loophole closures
the original-coined-hype-adjacent safe path as a guardrail
excluded: the trademark-clearance gate and the final name (naming KB owns)
the identity system

pros.claim: Carrying the legal hard-no as a guardrail keeps content and paid spend from ever attaching to a name that fee-shifting law could turn into a margin-ending lawsuit
pros.example: rejecting an athlete-nickname drop name before any content is produced, because 3344 fee-shifting alone can exceed the line's margin

cons.claim: An aggressive guardrail can over-block a genuinely cleared cultural reference that could have lived as a drop name
cons.example: killing a non-identity meme drop name that would have cleared, out of excess caution

failure_modes: letting content or paid spend reference an athlete/celebrity/event identity before clearance
assuming a dead celebrity or a local college athlete is a safe harbor (post-mortem and NIL close both)
acceptance_tests: the guardrail states the hard no on real athlete/celebrity/event/meme as house brand/drop/SKU, the 3344/3344.1/Lanham/Class-25 stack, the NIL and post-mortem loophole closures, and the original-coined-hype-adjacent safe path, blocking any pre-clearance name reference in content or spend
revisit_triggers: a candidate name or drop name is proposed for content or spend
the naming-clearance gate returns a result

base.update_signal: a candidate name is proposed or the clearance gate returns

nodes.definition: Assemble the consolidated go-to-market plan that turns the scattered channel, pricing, and signal decisions into one launch operating system: the contribution-ordered channel ladder with the load-bearing organic+hub+email/SMS tier and amplify-only paid; the bulk-import-then-US-fulfill operating posture; the three-article price ladder with A1 as the protected margin engine and the AOV target of ~$120-150 via bundles; the AOV/CAC-headroom test and the <~$35 blended-CAC discipline as the go/no-go precondition; the instrument-panel signals and the pinned hype-signal and size-curve preconditions; the marketplace and wholesale routing; and the naming legal guardrail. It is the single artifact the owner launches from and hands to the decision-brain layer, with every soft input labeled and the live $1-2k ad test named as the highest-leverage hardening move.

every soft input labeled with the ad-test hardening move
the hand-off to the decision-brain
excluded: the final viability go/no-go verdict (decision-brain owns)
the individual node decisions already made upstream

pros.claim: One consolidated plan converts a pile of channel and pricing decisions into an executable launch with no orphaned channel and the CAC precondition front and center
pros.example: a single launch sheet listing the ladder, posture, price/AOV target, CAC threshold, signals, and guardrail the owner executes from

nodes.definition: Define the loop that keeps the GTM plan alive: a fixed review cadence (a per-cycle signal read on the instrument panel plus a per-PO re-confirmation of the live duty and de-minimis state) and the material-change triggers that send the owner back through the upstream nodes to re-plan: a Central-Valley-youth trend shift, a live duty or surcharge change at a PO cycle, a blended-CAC drift above ~$35 (or a live ad test result), an A2 pilling-sentiment event, a hero-colour sell-through surprise, or a candidate name reaching clearance. Each trigger routes back to a named node (trend to HYPE_SIGNAL_PIN, duty to BULK_IMPORT_FULFILL, CAC to CAC_DISCIPLINE and AOV_CAC_HEADROOM, pilling to ORGANIC_SOCIAL_ENGINE). Without this loop the plan silently drifts out of cost, trend, and contribution alignment, since every governing input here is a moving estimate.

edge_cases.trigger: a public quality-failure video on the highest-return article
edge_cases.mitigation: promise only the QC pilling gate (>=3-4), never a fabricated percentage, and hold the acrylic to the contractual gate before content ships

edge_cases.description: A name or content calendar ships before the Central-Valley-youth hype signal is pinned
edge_cases.trigger: launch proceeds on a guessed trend no file owns
edge_cases.mitigation: gate any name or content calendar on a pinned hype signal via the trend-ingestion / AI-design pass

edge_cases.description: The brand names a drop or SKU after a real athlete/nickname/event and triggers right-of-publicity and false-endorsement exposure
edge_cases.trigger: a borrowed-identity name reaches content or paid spend
edge_cases.mitigation: block any real-identity name; use an original coined hype-adjacent registrable wordmark and clear it before any reference

edge_cases.description: A live ad test returns a blended CAC well above the ~$35 survival threshold
edge_cases.trigger: the single un-cross-examined CAC benchmark is tested and collapses
edge_cases.mitigation: shift the mix harder to organic/community/affiliate, raise AOV via bundles, and re-run the headroom test before scaling spend

edge_cases.description: A3 merino is listed on Amazon and the premium/AI story is commoditized
edge_cases.trigger: the premium article is placed on a mass marketplace
edge_cases.mitigation: keep A3 exclusive to the owned hub; route only A2 and a basic A1/A2 cash line to marketplaces

edge_cases.description: The A2 youth front door visually and verbally becomes the house brand and erodes the A1 margin engine
edge_cases.trigger: the transient front-door identity overtakes the durable core
edge_cases.mitigation: keep A1 the protected center of gravity and ensure the identity hard-codes neither a fibre nor a season

edge_cases.description: A live duty or India-surcharge change at a PO cycle re-floors the landed cost mid-plan
edge_cases.trigger: the volatile India duty moves between order cycles
edge_cases.mitigation: re-confirm the live duty and de-minimis state every PO and re-run the price ladder and headroom test

edge_cases.description: The uncalibrated size curve drives an online return rate above the carried band and erases contribution
edge_cases.trigger: scaling online before the Turlock pop-up size-curve fix runs
edge_cases.mitigation: fix the size curve in person at the Turlock seed and split returns by article and size before scaling

edge_cases.description: A bundle is discounted so deeply to lift AOV that per-unit contribution drops below the single-unit margin
edge_cases.trigger: an over-discounted bundle chases an AOV number
edge_cases.mitigation: bundle to lift AOV only where the basket still clears per-unit contribution

edge_cases.description: A CAC, conversion, or return benchmark is quoted downstream as a measured first-party figure
edge_cases.trigger: a labeled estimate loses its estimate tag in the hand-off
edge_cases.mitigation: carry every CAC/conversion/return figure as a labeled estimate with method and confidence and name the live ad test as the hardening move

workflow.description: Name the Turlock seed and the ship-to-CA scale shopper and the local-seed-to-social-scale posture
workflow.gate: the seed (near-zero CAC, size-curve fix) and the scale shopper (CAC kill-risk) are both named

workflow.description: State the de-minimis-repeal model-flip to bulk IOR into a CA 3PL with domestic ship
workflow.gate: the bulk-import-then-US-fulfill posture and the MPF-cap reinforcement are documented before channels

workflow.description: Order organic+hub+email/SMS as load-bearing, paid as amplify-only, marketplaces secondary, wholesale deferred
workflow.gate: the ladder is ordered by contribution survivability with each paid rung conditioned on organic

workflow.action: Set up the organic engine and owned hub
workflow.description: Build AI-design process content as earned media and route it into the Shopify hub and email/SMS list
workflow.gate: the organic engine is load-bearing with the no-pill claim promised as the QC gate

workflow.action: Set the price ladder and story pillars
workflow.description: Position A2 front door / A1 margin engine / A3 halo and the three story pillars
workflow.gate: A1 is the protected center of gravity and the bands are tagged positioning-not-a-model

workflow.description: Recompute per-order contribution and the CAC ceiling from AOV with labeled inputs
workflow.gate: the formula outputs a per-config contribution and CAC ceiling band that tightens with an ad test

workflow.action: Set the bundle AOV lever and CAC discipline
workflow.description: Lift AOV to ~$120-150 via bundles and hold blended CAC under ~$35 organic-heavy
workflow.gate: the AOV target ~$120-150 and the <~$35 blended-CAC precondition are set

workflow.action: Route marketplaces and the wholesale pilot
workflow.description: Route A2 to Etsy/TikTok-Shop, basic cash line to Amazon, never A3 on Amazon, defer wholesale
workflow.gate: each article is routed or blocked per the rules and wholesale is gated on a confirmed margin floor

workflow.action: Set the demand panel and pin the hype signal
workflow.description: Enumerate the watch signals and flag the Central-Valley-youth hype signal as the [UNKNOWN] to pin
workflow.gate: the panel is enumerated and the hype signal is flagged as owned by no file, gating name/content

workflow.description: State the hard no on a real athlete/celebrity/event/meme name and the coined hype-adjacent safe path
workflow.gate: no content or spend may reference a name before clearance; the hard-no and safe path are stated

workflow.description: Integrate ladder, posture, price/AOV, CAC test, signals, routing, and guardrail into one launch plan
workflow.gate: every channel is routed, the CAC/AOV precondition is central, and soft inputs are labeled

workflow.action: Set the GTM review cadence and triggers
workflow.description: Define the per-cycle signal and per-PO duty review and the material-change triggers back to upstream nodes
workflow.gate: a cadence and an explicit trigger list routing to named nodes exist

dominance_rules.rule: The naming legal hard-no dominates any hype-driven naming or content idea
dominance_rules.rationale: right-of-publicity fee-shifting plus false-endorsement plus class-25 marks can produce a bill exceeding the line's whole margin, and any one is enough to lose
dominance_rules.trigger: a name or drop references a real athlete/celebrity/event/meme identity
dominance_rules.action: block it; use an original coined hype-adjacent registrable wordmark and clear it before any reference

dominance_rules.rule: The contribution-after-CAC test dominates gross-margin or reach optimization
dominance_rules.rationale: an 80-86% gross margin is a trap; the order only survives if it pays its own CAC, which gross margin ignores
dominance_rules.trigger: a channel or pricing choice optimizes reach or gross margin without checking post-CAC contribution
dominance_rules.action: run the AOV/CAC-headroom test and keep paid amplify-only until the config clears it

dominance_rules.rule: The pinned hype signal dominates shipping a name or content calendar
dominance_rules.rationale: both a hype-adjacent name and trend-native content depend on a live signal that no upstream file owns
dominance_rules.trigger: a name or content calendar is about to ship on a guessed trend
dominance_rules.action: gate the ship on a pinned hype signal from the trend-ingestion / AI-design pass

dominance_rules.rule: The QC pilling gate dominates any anti-pill marketing claim
dominance_rules.rationale: a fabricated percentage the gate cannot defend invites returns and a brand-ending pilling video on the acrylic
dominance_rules.trigger: content promises an anti-pill number stronger than the contractual gate
dominance_rules.action: promise only the ICI pilling gate (>=3-4 post-wash), never a fabricated percentage

dominance_rules.rule: The bulk-import posture dominates any drop-ship channel design
dominance_rules.rationale: the de-minimis repeal killed duty-free per-order import and the MPF floor punishes per-parcel entry
dominance_rules.trigger: a channel or marketplace flow assumes per-order import from Ludhiana
dominance_rules.action: route everything through the bulk IOR into a CA 3PL with domestic ship

dominance_rules.rule: Protecting the A1 margin engine dominates pushing the A2 front door
dominance_rules.rationale: if the transient youth front door becomes the house brand, both the margin and the brand's longevity erode
dominance_rules.trigger: the A2 identity is about to overtake the durable core
dominance_rules.action: keep A1 the protected center of gravity and never let the front door become the whole house

dominance_rules.rule: Never listing A3 on Amazon dominates the reach gain of doing so
dominance_rules.rationale: a mass marketplace commoditizes the premium/AI story that is the brand's whole defensible position
dominance_rules.trigger: the premium article is proposed for a mass marketplace
dominance_rules.action: keep A3 to the owned hub; route only A2 and a basic cash line to marketplaces

dominance_rules.rule: The live duty re-confirmation dominates a locked price or contribution plan
dominance_rules.rationale: the India duty is high and volatile, so a price ladder or headroom result hardens into error if not re-priced per PO
dominance_rules.trigger: an order cycle proceeds on a stale duty assumption
dominance_rules.action: re-confirm the live duty and de-minimis state every PO and re-run the price and headroom

dominance_rules.rule: The review loop dominates an impulse channel or content pivot
dominance_rules.rationale: structured review prevents churning the content cadence and channel mix on a transient signal wobble
dominance_rules.trigger: a tempting trend or price signal appears mid-cycle
dominance_rules.action: evaluate it through the review loop's triggers, not on impulse

anti_rework_rules.rule: Clear the naming legal guardrail before any content or paid spend references a name
anti_rework_rules.prevents: producing content or buying ads around a name that fee-shifting law can turn into a margin-ending lawsuit

anti_rework_rules.rule: Pin the Central-Valley-youth hype signal before shipping a name or content calendar
anti_rework_rules.prevents: launching a hype-adjacent name and a content cadence on a guessed trend no file owns and re-doing both

anti_rework_rules.rule: Fix the bulk-import operating posture before designing any channel or marketplace flow
anti_rework_rules.prevents: building a channel system around a dead duty-free drop-ship model and re-architecting fulfillment

anti_rework_rules.rule: Run the AOV/CAC-headroom test before turning on any paid spend
anti_rework_rules.prevents: buying cold customers at a CAC a sub-$90 order cannot pay and burning the launch budget

anti_rework_rules.rule: Promise only the QC pilling gate, never a fabricated percentage, before any content ships
anti_rework_rules.prevents: a return spike and a brand-ending pilling video from an undefendable claim

anti_rework_rules.rule: Set the AOV target to ~$120-150 via bundles before pricing single units as heroes
anti_rework_rules.prevents: selling single $55 sweaters that cannot pay a realistic CAC and re-pricing after losses

anti_rework_rules.rule: Fix the size curve at the Turlock seed before scaling online
anti_rework_rules.prevents: scaling an uncalibrated fit and eating a return rate above the carried band

anti_rework_rules.rule: Label every CAC, conversion, and return figure as an estimate when first written
anti_rework_rules.prevents: a benchmark being quoted downstream as a measured first-party fact and mis-grounding the verdict

anti_rework_rules.rule: Re-confirm the live duty and de-minimis state before each PO and each price-ladder lock
anti_rework_rules.prevents: hardening a stale duty into the price and contribution plan and re-flooring everything later

iteration_protocol.trigger: a live ad test returns a real blended CAC
iteration_protocol.action: re-run the headroom test, re-set the acquisition mix, and update the CAC discipline and plan

iteration_protocol.trigger: a Central-Valley-youth trend shift or a trend-ingestion pass lands
iteration_protocol.action: re-pin the hype signal and refresh the name lane and content calendar

iteration_protocol.trigger: a live duty or India-surcharge change at a PO cycle
iteration_protocol.action: re-confirm the posture, re-floor the price ladder, and re-run the headroom test

iteration_protocol.trigger: an A2 pilling-sentiment or quality-failure event surfaces on social
iteration_protocol.action: tighten the QC-gate claim, manage the content response, and re-check the acrylic return rate

iteration_protocol.trigger: a candidate brand or drop name reaches the clearance gate
iteration_protocol.action: re-run the naming legal guardrail before attaching any content or spend

iteration_protocol.trigger: the in-person size-curve calibration completes or first-cohort returns arrive
iteration_protocol.action: split returns by article and size and re-run the headroom test with the real returns load

iteration_protocol.trigger: a content piece proves organic performance worth amplifying
iteration_protocol.action: turn on amplify-only paid behind it on a headroom-clearing config

iteration_protocol.trigger: the unit_economics layer confirms a wholesale margin floor
iteration_protocol.action: re-test the deferred wholesale pilot for the A1/A3 articles

priority_rationale: The two-market consumer split and the bulk-import operating posture come first because every channel and pricing choice depends on knowing who is being acquired where and that the fulfillment model is bulk-import-then-US-fulfill, not dead duty-free drop-ship; the channel ladder and its channel nodes (organic, owned hub, amplify-only paid, marketplaces, wholesale) build the acquisition system on top; the price ladder, story pillars, AOV/CAC-headroom formula, bundle lever, and CAC discipline compose the economics that decide whether an order pays for its own customer; the signals, the pinned hype-signal, the returns/size-curve, and the naming legal guardrail are the watch-and-guardrail layer; and the consolidated plan and the review loop come last because they compose everything into one launch artifact and route material trend, duty, and CAC changes back to the foundations.
